newsitem.title: UK: London gold stable in Europe, ponders next move.
newsitem.headline: London gold stable in Europe, ponders next move.

text.p: The gold market hovered below the key $330 mark on Tuesday and dealers said failure to break above that level soon could signal another return to the downside.
Gold prices had rallied last Friday in response to a sharp decline in U.S. stock and bond markets on Friday.
But Wall Street's better performance on Monday diminished the chances that gold could summon up enough support to push higher for now, dealers said.
Gold was fixed at $327.60 an ounce, virtually unchanged from $327.70 on Monday afternoon. But prices were off the firmer New York close of $328.20/$328.70.
The market will watch U.S. economic data due out later this week for signs that inflation is on the rise, analysts said.

"Any signs that inflation is picking up will give the market further support...In any case there is no point getting too positive unless there is a convincing break of resistance at $330," brokers GNI said in a report.
Turnover in the precious metals was light in early trading, lulled by the August slowdown, and any sharp moves would unlikely to emerge during European trading hours, dealers said.

But the platinum group metals were sharply lower after late Monday's news that a week-old strike at South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd had ended after a deal was struck with more than 400 striking workers at the platinum refineries.
Impala said production had not been affected and some 400 striking workers returned to work on Tuesday morning.
Dealers said the week-long strike had helped underpin the price, but the settlement would not do more than bruise sentiment.
"While there may well be further negative reaction today, the market remains fundamentally tight which will help limit the downside," GNI said.
Supplies of platinum and palladium remain tight as long-delayed exports from chief producer Russia have been small and demand is strong, dealers said.
Platinum was last indicated at $436.00/$439.00, down $8 from Monday's London close.
Palladium, which had soared to 17-year highs last week, was down slightly as well at $227.00/$232.00, compared to $231.60/$234.60 at Monday's close.
Silver prices were stuck in a narrow range and last quoted just one cent firmer at $4.43/$4.45 an ounce.
